top3.headline: Dario Amodei shares his remarks on Anthropic's IPO
top3.whyItMatters: A frontier lab's CEO now speaks to public shareholders, and his framing sets expectations for the sector.

top3.headline: PrimeIntellect appears compromised; OpenRouter warned affected users
top3.whyItMatters: A breach at one model provider can reach every agent and team that routes through it.

top3.headline: Perplexity Computer now writes and updates agent skills from past sessions
top3.whyItMatters: Agents that improve their own playbooks lower the cost of keeping AI workflows current.

items.title: Perplexity adds prompt-injection checks to its Context API
items.takeaway: After feedback from Tobi, Perplexity shipped decision models that screen fetched content for prompt injection and score it on custom criteria.
items.soWhat: Web content is a main route for attacking agents, so filtering it before use is basic hygiene.

items.title: Dario Amodei shares his remarks on Anthropic's IPO
items.takeaway: Anthropic posted CEO Dario Amodei's remarks on its IPO. He opens with why he and his co-founders started the company.
items.soWhat: A frontier lab's CEO now speaks to public shareholders, so mission claims meet market scrutiny.

items.title: Perplexity Computer now writes its own agent skills from past sessions
items.takeaway: Brain, which keeps a wiki about your work, now writes and updates agent skills; an improvement agent reads full session trajectories.
items.soWhat: Agents that learn from their own sessions cut the manual work of maintaining skills.

items.title: PrimeIntellect appears compromised; OpenRouter alerted affected users
items.takeaway: Theo says PrimeIntellect appears compromised in a 'very strange way'. No public word from PrimeIntellect yet; OpenRouter told affected users, him included.
items.soWhat: Each model provider behind your agents is part of your security surface, so track who you depend on.

items.title: Meng To: Claude Code built four 3D game characters on its own
items.takeaway: For a three.js game Fable 5.2 built in 2 days, he gave Claude Code a picture of each character plus the Hi3D MCP.
items.soWhat: Agents with the right tool connectors can now produce design assets, not just code.

items.title: Perplexity says Multiagent usage doubled in a single day
items.takeaway: Users pick it for work that splits into parallel pieces: decks, multi-source research, financial analysis, contact lists. Perplexity also shipped Monitor, Orchestrator and Context APIs.
items.soWhat: Parallel agent work is finding real demand in everyday knowledge tasks, not just coding.

items.title: Simon Willison's pelican test shows effort levels change results
items.takeaway: He compares Gemini 4 Carbon, Neon and Hydrogen at low, medium and high effort on one drawing test.
items.soWhat: Effort settings are a cost and quality dial worth testing before you standardize on a model.

items.title: Theo gives each model a role inside T3 Code
items.takeaway: Fable leads implementation, GPT-6.2 Astra playtests and Gemini 4 Neon writes copy, each in its native harness and subscription.
items.soWhat: Teams can assign models by strength instead of betting everything on one vendor.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro turns five concept images into a 3D house site
items.takeaway: From five concept images it built the Blender model, materials and light, then a scroll-driven site cut open floor by floor.
items.soWhat: Concept-to-client walkthrough is collapsing from weeks of studio work into one agent session.

items.title: Genie 4 lets users reshape a generated world while exploring it
items.takeaway: Users can type prompts mid-exploration to add characters or change the scene, with audio adapting live; available to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers.
items.soWhat: Interactive world models point to new formats for training, simulation and product demos.

items.title: Cursor adds Gemini 4 Neon, scoring 63.7% on CursorBench 4.1
items.takeaway: At default effort Neon scores 63.7% on CursorBench 4.1, up from 57.3% for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, at $3/M input and $15/M output tokens.
items.soWhat: Better coding scores at mid-tier prices lower the cost of putting agents on real engineering work.

items.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, Nasdaq trading next
items.takeaway: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share; the SEC declared its registration effective on November 18 and Nasdaq trading is expected November 19.
items.soWhat: A frontier lab now answers to public markets, so its pace and risk choices get priced daily.

image.alt: @AnthropicAI on X: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, Nasdaq trading next

items.title: Tavi Costa sees silver miners in a capitulation phase
items.takeaway: Record outflows from the sector's biggest ETF, down more than 50% in six months; he says doubting your thesis is normal now.
items.soWhat: A reminder that conviction is tested hardest when flows run the other way.

items.title: OpenAI: AI use by its own researchers keeps rising exponentially
items.takeaway: OpenAI shares new data: researchers' AI use keeps rising exponentially, agents complete longer tasks, humans stay central, and researchers spend more time on safety.
items.soWhat: How a frontier lab uses agents today previews how expert teams will work next.

items.title: ThePrimeagen: Sol set up sign-in across five services in 5 minutes
items.takeaway: ThePrimeagen told Sol to use his computer to create tokens for Cloudflare, YouTube, Twitch, Kick and X and make sign-in work locally and in production.
items.soWhat: Agents that operate your computer can now clear tedious setup work in minutes.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon models a 3D lab scene through Blender MCP
items.takeaway: Sundar Pichai shows Gemini 4 Neon 3D-modeling a photorealistic lab simulation in Antigravity via Blender MCP.
items.soWhat: Design tools are becoming something agents drive directly, not just something people click.

items.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Neon for engineering, knowledge work and science
items.takeaway: Gemini 4 Neon sits between Carbon and Hydrogen and rolls out today in the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Gemini for business and paid AI Pro and Ultra.
items.soWhat: Google's fourth Gemini 4 model this month keeps the price and quality race moving.

items.title: David Sacks: Anthropic sells 'closing the loop' on its IPO roadshow
items.takeaway: Sacks argues Anthropic is racing toward recursive self-improvement faster than any lab. The Atlantic calls it the reluctant winner; Gary Marcus asks if the IPO is a bad bet.
items.soWhat: Anthropic's IPO is turning its safety stance into a public debate over speed and risk.

items.title: Benaich: Abundant Labs launches a test for self-improving models
items.takeaway: Nathan Benaich says Abundant Labs launched FrontierRSI, which tests whether a model can achieve recursive self-improvement.
items.soWhat: Self-improvement is moving from debate to something investors want measured.

items.title: The Verge asks what Nvidia is without Jensen Huang in charge
items.takeaway: The Verge, on Nvidia's earnings: 'What is Nvidia without AI's sugar daddy in charge?'
items.soWhat: Leadership risk at the main AI chip supplier is now part of the compute story.

items.title: Benaich: what would a genius bar for AI look like?
items.takeaway: Benaich imagines giving a small business owner, a busy family or a healthcare provider an hour with someone who shows them what AI can do for their own work.
items.soWhat: Adoption may hinge on hands-on help with real work, not better models alone.

items.title: Microsoft and Perplexity both pitch AI as the OS for work
items.takeaway: Nadella says Salesforce is coming to Copilot 'as we build Copilot as the OS for work'. Perplexity puts Teammates and Multiagent on mobile, calling it 'a mini workOS'.
items.soWhat: The fight is shifting from best model to which assistant owns the daily workspace.
